us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.source: NMHC and NAA rent-control preemption tracking (2022-2025), Virginia Housing Commission study (June 2026), state code sites and Justia for each statute; searched 2026-09-28.
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.note: No with preempts false: no statewide limit, and cities may set their own. Places first left out were read on 9/29/2026; any still unread take the most common answer among similar places, marked ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE.

US-AK.cite: Alaska Stat. ch. 34.03 (Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
US-AK.note: Alaska's landlord-tenant act sets no rent limit and has no bar on local rent control, and AS 34.03.310(a)(4) even protects tenants who complain to agencies enforcing governmental rent controls.

US-AS.estimated: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: the most common answer among the 2 territories read for this question (2 answer no), because this place's own law could not be read.
US-AS.note: Tried: American Samoa Code Annotated at https://asbar.org/ (HTTP 403 bot block, section search unreachable); https://www.asbar.org/ (no connection); web.archive.org (no snapshot); https://www.americansamoa.gov/ (script-rendered site with no code text); constituteproject.org (404).

US-AZ.note: Preemption dates from 1981 and covers charter cities.

US-CA.cite: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (AB 1482, Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
US-CA.note: Caps increases at 5% plus local CPI or 10%, whichever is lower, on most units 15+ years old; exempts qualifying owner-noticed single-family homes and condos; sunsets 2030-01-01.

US-CO.note: HB23-1115, which would have repealed the preemption, passed the House in 2023 but did not become law.

US-CT.note: Towns may, and towns of 25,000 or more must, create fair rent commissions that can cut an excessive rent or increase case by case, but there is no annual numeric cap.

US-DC.note: District-wide rent stabilization covers most pre-1976 units: CPI-W plus 2%, capped at 10%, once per 12 months; lower cap for registered elderly or disabled tenants.

US-DE.cite: 25 Del. C. ch. 51 et seq. (Residential Landlord-Tenant Code)
US-DE.note: Delaware's landlord-tenant code sets no general rent-increase limit and neither it nor the home-rule limits in 22 Del. C. § 835 bar local rent control; the rent-justification law covers only manufactured-home lot rents.

US-FL.note: The 2023 Live Local Act removed the former housing-emergency exception effective 2023-07-01.

US-GU.cite: 21 GCA ch. 48 (Guam Landlord and Tenant Rental Act of 2018)
US-GU.note: The Guam landlord-tenant act sets deposits, notices and remedies but contains no rent limit or rent-increase cap, so Guam has no rent stabilization.

US-HI.cite: Haw. Rev. Stat. ch. 521 (Residential Landlord-Tenant Code)
US-HI.note: The state consumer-protection handbook says there is no limit on the amount of a rent increase because there is no rent control in Hawaii, and no statute barring county rent control was found.

US-IL.note: Enacted 1997; repeal bills (e.g., SB 1260, 2025) have not passed.

US-KY.note: Only the General Assembly may enact rent control on private property.

US-LA.note: Lessor rights may not be altered except by state law (Acts 1977, No. 655); it is an implied rather than rent-specific preemption.

US-MA.cite: Mass. G.L. c. 40P (Rent Control Prohibition Act, 1994 Question 9)
US-MA.note: The Supreme Judicial Court removed a 2026 rent-control initiative from the ballot.

US-MD.cite: Montgomery County rent stabilization law (county ordinance, 2023)
US-MD.note: Maryland has no statewide cap, and Montgomery County runs an Office of Rent Stabilization that limits increases on licensed rental units at least 23 years old.

US-ME.cite: Portland, Me., rent control ordinance (November 2020 referendum)
US-ME.note: Maine has no statewide cap, and Portland voters adopted a local ordinance that limits annual rent increases.

US-MN.note: Local rent control is prohibited unless voters approve it at a general election, which St. Paul and Minneapolis have done, so cities may act only by referendum.

US-MO.note: Preemption was broadened in August 2025 to other landlord-tenant topics.

US-MP.note: The Commonwealth Code has no rent limit or rent-increase cap and does not bar local rent rules, so the Northern Mariana Islands has no statewide rent stabilization.

US-MS.note: Municipalities may not regulate residential rent without prior legislative approval.

US-MT.note: Express denial of local rent-control power added in 2023 (sources name SB 105 or HB 463); opponents said it was already prohibited.

US-NE.note: Signed 2025-04-07; takes effect three months after the 2025 session adjourned (operative date computed, not stated in results).

US-NH.cite: N.H. RSA 31:39; RSA 47:17 (enumerated bylaw powers; no grant over rents); RSA 540, 540-A (no rent-limit provision)
US-NH.note: Weak: no statute bars local rent limits, but New Hampshire follows Dillon's Rule and no statute gives towns or cities power over rents.

US-NJ.cite: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5 (30-year new-construction exemption); municipal police power (Helmsley v. Borough of Fort Lee, 78 N.J. 200 (1978))
US-NJ.note: The state Department of Community Affairs says New Jersey has no state law controlling rents and municipalities may pass rent control or rent leveling ordinances, with new construction exempt for 30 years.

US-NV.cite: Nev. Rev. Stat. ch. 118A (NRS 118A.300 notice of rent increase)
US-NV.note: Nevada's landlord-tenant chapter requires only 60 days' notice of a rent increase and contains no bar on local rent control.

US-NY.cite: Emergency Tenant Protection Act of 1974 (local opt-in)
US-NY.note: The state ETPA lets a municipality adopt rent stabilization after declaring a local housing emergency, so limits apply only in New York City and opt-in localities.

US-OH.note: HB 430 added an express preemption of local rent control and rent stabilization.

US-OR.note: Cap is 7% plus CPI; SB 611 (effective 2023-07-06) added a 10% ceiling; units under 15 years old are exempt; ORS 91.225 still preempts local rent control.
US-OR.constructionQuote: The first certificate of occupancy for the dwelling unit was issued less than 15 years from the date of the notice of the rent increase.

phases.cite: ORS 90.323 and 90.324; Oregon Office of Economic Analysis 2026 maximum annual rent increase
phases.sourceQuote: The allowable rent increase percentage for the previous year, 2026, was 9.5%.
phases.note: The annual cap replaces the ceiling scalar for this calendar year. The 15-year construction exemption remains. ORS 90.323(5)(b) also exempts specified regulated-affordable rent changes; recorded tenancy regimes do not establish every exemption fact.

phases.cite: ORS 90.323 and 90.324; Oregon Office of Economic Analysis 2027 maximum annual rent increase
phases.sourceQuote: For 2027, the maximum allowable rent increase percentage for tenancies subject to ORS 90.324(b) is 10%.
phases.note: The annual cap replaces the ceiling scalar for this calendar year. The 15-year construction exemption remains. ORS 90.323(5)(b) also exempts specified regulated-affordable rent changes; recorded tenancy regimes do not establish every exemption fact.

US-PA.note: Weak: no statute bans rent control, but the home-rule law and Dillon's Rule keep cities from capping rents.

Laws Ann. tit. 17 rent-regulation statute (Ley de Alquileres Razonables, Ley 464 of 1946) not located: LexJuris yearly law menus 1990-2026 list no rent-control law or repeal (lexjuris.com/lexlex/Leyes<year>/lexl<year>Menu.htm); Ley 132-2011 (repeal of Ley 142-1968) is a building-maintenance law, not rent control; bvirtualogp.pr.gov PDFs 404; the pre-1990 statute text could not be reached.

US-RI.note: Rhode Island requires only 60 days' notice of a rent increase (120 days for month-to-month tenants over 62) and has no statute barring local rent control.

US-TX.note: Cities may impose rent control only in a disaster-declared housing emergency with the governor's approval.

US-UT.note: Local rent control requires express legislative approval.

US-VA.cite: Va. Code § 55.1-1200 et seq. (VRLTA supersession) with Dillon Rule
US-VA.note: No rent-specific preemption statute; localities lack authority because the VRLTA supersedes local landlord-tenant ordinances, and 2026 bills HB 278/SB 355 to authorize local rent regulation were sent to study.

US-VT.note: Vermont's rental chapter, current through the 2025 session, has no rent cap and no bar on local rent control, though a city would need a charter change approved by the legislature.

US-WA.constructionQuote: A tenancy in a dwelling unit for which the first certificate of occupancy was issued 12 or less years before the date of the notice of the rent increase.
US-WA.note: Cap is the lesser of 7% plus CPI or 10% over 12 months (9.683% for 2026); RCW 59.18.710(1)(a): first certificate of occupancy issued 12 or less years before notice is exempt; expires 2040-07-01; RCW 35.21.830 still preempts local rent control.

phases.cite: RCW 59.18.700; Washington Department of Commerce 2026 maximum annual rent increase
phases.sourceQuote: Maximum annual rent increase percent through 12/31/2026: 9.683%
phases.note: The announced calendar-year maximum replaces the statutory ceiling scalar. The sourced 12-year construction exemption remains; RCW 59.18.710 contains additional property and landlord exemptions not established by a tenancy regime alone.

phases.cite: RCW 59.18.700; Washington Department of Commerce 2027 maximum annual rent increase
phases.sourceQuote: Maximum annual rent increase percent through 12/31/2027: 10%
phases.note: The announced calendar-year maximum replaces the statutory ceiling scalar. The sourced 12-year construction exemption remains; RCW 59.18.710 contains additional property and landlord exemptions not established by a tenancy regime alone.

US-WV.note: Cities hold only the powers the code lists, and the list in § 8-12-5 (read 9/28/2026) grants no power over rents; its item (43) is a general welfare clause. The home rule section adds that municipalities "may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property" (§ 8-1-5a(k)). So a typical city may not set rent limits.

US-WY.cite: Wyo. Stat. §§ 1-21-1201 to -1211 (Residential Rental Property Act)
US-WY.note: No rent-control preemption appears in Wyoming's landlord-tenant, municipal (Title 15) or property (Title 34) statutes as compiled in May 2026, so the claim of a preemption statute is unsupported.

Code 65852.21, RCW 36.70A.635, 30-A M.R.S. 4364-A, MCA 76-2-304, 24 V.S.A. 4412, A.R.S. 9-462.13; Montana Free Press (3/3/2025, 3/18/2026) on the SB 323 litigation; 'no' answers rest on each state's own zoning statute or section list (weak) because no complete current tracker fetched (Terner Center 2/2023 database is self-described as not comprehensive).
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.all.note: Places first left out were read on 9/29/2026; any still unread take the most common answer among similar places, marked ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE.

US-AK.note: Weak: No state law requires cities to allow duplexes or more on single-family lots (Pew, 9/15/2025, lists no such law here); cities set their own zoning.

US-AL.note: Weak: No state law requires cities to allow duplexes or more on single-family lots (Pew, 9/15/2025, lists no such law here); cities set their own zoning.

US-AR.cite: Ark. Code § 14-56-416 (2025 Ark. Act 313 is ADU only)
US-AR.note: Weak: Arkansas Act 313 of 2025 requires accessory dwelling units on single-family lots only, and no state law requires duplexes or more; cities set their own zoning.

US-AS.note: American Samoa's single dwelling (R1) zone permits only one-family dwellings and their accessory uses, so duplexes are not allowed by right there.

US-AZ.note: Cities of 75,000 or more must allow duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes and townhomes as a permitted use on all single-family lots within one mile of the central business district (and on 20% of new developments over 10 acres) by 1/1/2026; a city that misses the deadline must allow middle housing on all single-family lots.

US-CA.note: Every city and county must approve up to two units on a single-family lot ministerially, without a hearing, in urbanized areas (with a companion lot-split rule allowing up to four units); the fetched text reflects a 2026 amendment (SB 1426) that did not change the 1/1/2026 answer.

US-CO.note: Weak: HB24-1313 sets transit-area zoning-capacity goals (average 40 units per acre) for transit-oriented communities and HB24-1152 covers accessory dwelling units only; neither requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-CT.note: Connecticut H.B. 8002 (signed 11/26/2025) rewards towns that add housing near transit and downtowns but leaves residential zoning to each town, so no state law requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-DC.note: There is no state layer: the District's own Zoning Commission writes its zoning regulations, so no higher law requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-DE.note: Weak: No state law requires cities to allow duplexes or more on single-family lots (Pew, 9/15/2025, lists no such law here); cities set their own zoning.

US-FL.note: Weak: Florida law requires multifamily housing only in commercial, industrial and mixed-use zones (Live Local Act), and no state law requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-GA.note: Weak: No state law requires cities to allow duplexes or more on single-family lots (Pew, 9/15/2025, lists no such law here); cities set their own zoning.

US-GU.note: Guam's zoning law permits only one-family dwellings (and accessory units) by right in the R1 zone, and duplexes there need conditional-use approval.

US-HI.cite: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 46-4 (2025 H.B. 1409 is transit-area only)
US-HI.note: Weak: Hawaii H.B. 1409 (2025) rewards counties that allow apartments near transit, but no state law requires duplexes or more on single-family lots.

US-TX.cite: Tex. Loc. Gov't Code ch. 211 (2025 S.B. 15 and S.B. 840)
US-TX.note: Weak: Texas S.B. 15 (2025) allows single-family homes on 3,000-square-foot lots in new subdivisions and S.B. 840 allows apartments in commercial zones, but neither requires duplexes on existing single-family lots.

US-UT.note: Utah H.B. 37 (2025) only authorizes cities and counties to allow more density in exchange for affordability terms, and no state law requires duplexes or more on single-family lots.

US-VA.note: Weak: The state's planning and zoning chapter (section list) contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-VI.cite: V.I. Code tit. 29, § 228 (table of permitted uses, R-1)
US-VI.note: The territorial zoning table lets two-family dwellings be built as of right in the R-1 low-density residential zone beside single-family homes, and it has no single-family-only zone (read from the 2019 codification).

US-VT.note: Every municipality must allow a duplex in any district that allows year-round residential use, on the same lot size as a single-unit home, and in districts served by municipal water and sewer must allow up to four units (source history: 2023, No. 47, § 2, eff. July 1, 2023).

US-WA.note: Cities of 25,000 to 75,000 must allow at least two units per residential lot (four near major transit or with an affordable unit), and cities of 75,000 or more must allow four (six near transit or with affordable units); each city must comply at its next periodic comprehensive plan update, so a few smaller or later-cycle cities may not yet have been bound on 1/1/2026.

US-WV.note: Weak: The state's zoning article contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-WY.note: Weak: The state's cities and towns title contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.
